The gas extraction process involves melting of large quantities of ice <u>in situ</u> and extracting the gases from the meltwater. These gases are then collected at the surface and are transported back to the laboratory for analysis.
The final hole planned, the access hole, will be a 30-cm diameter hole drilled through the ice shelf. This hole will be drilled using air first, and then meltwater, as a drilling fluid. After the shelf is penetrated the hole will be maintained with a diameter of 25-cm by use of an electrical heating cable.
Biological and oceanographic experiments in the seawater will be conducted through the access hole. A multi-purpose cable will be utilized for lowering instruments, operating underwater cameras, and for recovering seabottom samples. About one and one-half months will be available for these experiments.
The heating cable with some instrumentation attached will be allowed to freeze into the hole at the end of the season's operation. It is anticipated that during the subsequent field season it will be possible to melt the cable out to recover the instruments.
The RISP drilling operation will require the construction and maintenance of a field camp capable of supporting up to 35 people for a period of four (4) months. Jamesway buts will be utilized as the basic structures. Disposal of the various types of wastes from this camp is discussed in following sections of this report.
